text.p: Stocks rose Tuesday, aided by strength in bonds, as the market defied widespread fears of a near-term correction.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 23.48 points at 6,370.39 after Monday's dip of slightly more than one point ended the index's eight-session string of record high closes.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 12-9 on modest volume of 261 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 1.09 points at 1,255.66, and the American Stock Exchange index rose 0.71 at 584.89.
Many analysts had expected a pullback for stocks as investors reaped profits from the Dow's winning streak, but the rally in bonds helped reinforce the bullishness.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond rose 15/32, lowering its yield to 6.43 percent from 6.47 percent at Monday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Bonds gained after October housing starts fell for the second month in a row, reaching their lowest levels in more than a year, and provided further proof that the economy is slowing.
Wall Street likes the prospect of a steadily slowing "Goldilocks" economy -- meaning not too hot and not too cold -- because it raises prospects for steady or lower interest rates.
Gregory Nie, an analyst at EVEREN Securities said the market's upward move was surprising and that it was moving into overbought territory.
He said that the stock market's strong volume was counteracting the likelihood of a near-term correction.
"To counteract the overbought status, you need heavy firepower, and it has been impressive so far today," Nie said. "We've got a good shot at reaching 500 million shares."
"Volume has been a friend of the bull trend dating back to late 1994. It really has been part and parcel of the trend," he said.

Among individual shares, Hewlett-Packard rose 1 to 51-1/8 after analysts said they expected the computer maker to post stronger results. After Monday's close, Hewlett-Packard reported slightly lower than expected profits for its fiscal fourth quarter but said order growth was improving.
BankAmerica rose 2-5/8 to 98-5/8 and touched a new 52-week high of 99-5/8 after it announced a stock option plan for its 85,000 employees.
AlliedSignal jumped 1-5/8 to 72-5/8 after Goldman Sachs added the company to its priority list, according to a market source.
